Residency thesis &middot; BAP04-B-2026-6538 &middot; KAEK 2025/601 &middot; [in preparation]{.status .pending}\
Replication of Adams et al. (2018) Dataset 2 &middot; n=120 (60 schizophrenia + 60 controls) &middot; Two sessions\
Supervisor &middot; Prof. Dr. Gökhan Sarısoy &middot; Ondokuz Mayıs University
:::
:::

Two accounts of delusion sit side by side in the literature and are rarely
tested in the same people. One says beliefs are revised on too little
evidence. The other says self-generated sensation is not attenuated, so
ordinary actions carry the weight of external events.

This is a replication of Adams et al. (2018) Dataset 2, running both paradigms
in the same participants: a beads task modelled with the Hierarchical Gaussian
Filter to test belief updating, and a force-matching task on a device built for
this protocol to test sensory attenuation. Sixty people with schizophrenia and
sixty healthy controls, frequency-matched on age, sex, and education. Model and
parameter recovery were run before data collection. The analysis plan is
written; public registration is pending.

The [force-matching rig](../tools/force-matching.qmd) was designed and machined
in-house, because no manufacturer sells one. Running this paradigm means
building the instrument first.
